# CollabSphere  
Real-time collaborative editing tool for SaaS teams, built with WebSockets and Web Components to enable seamless document co-authoring across distributed teams  

[![GitHub](https://badgen.net/badge/github/valentinas-projects/1478a8)](https://github.com/valentinas-projects/collabsphere)  
[![npm](https://badgen.net/badge/npm/1.2.3/3366cc)](https://npmjs.com/package/collabsphere)  
[![Web Components](https://badgen.net/badge/web-components/1.2.3/2962ff)](https://webcomponents.org/)  

## Tech Stack  
- **Frontend**: React (18.x), TypeScript (4.9), Web Components (Lit 3), Tailwind CSS (3.x)  
- **Backend**: Node.js (18.x), Express (4.x), REST API (v1)  
- **Real-time**: WebSocket (Socket.io 4.x), Operational Transform (OT)  
- **Tools**: Webpack (5.x), ESLint (8.x), Prettier (3.x)  
- **Deployment**: Docker (24.x), GitHub Actions (v3)  

## Architecture / Design  
CollabSphere’s architecture prioritizes modularity and real-time synchronization. The core editor is built with Web Components to ensure cross-framework compatibility, while React handles the UI layer for declarative state management. WebSocket channels manage document deltas, with OT algorithms ensuring conflict-free updates. REST APIs handle metadata and user permissions, integrated with a PostgreSQL database for persistent storage.  

Responsive design is baked into the component tree, with a flexible grid system and dynamic font scaling. Performance optimizations include lazy-loaded modules and WebSocket connection pooling, reducing latency for 15+ concurrent editors.  

## Getting Started / Installation  
1. Clone the repo:  
   ```bash  
   git clone https://github.com/valentinas-projects/collabsphere.git  
   cd collabsphere  
   ```  
2. Install dependencies:  
   ```bash  
   npm install  
   ```  
3. Configure environment variables in `.env.local` for backend URL and API keys.  
4. Build the app:  
   ```bash  
   npm run build  
   ```  
5. Run tests:  
   ```bash  
   npm test  
   ```  

## Usage / Examples  
Launch a session via the `/dashboard` route. Click "New Document" to create a shared workspace. Real-time changes appear instantly across all connected clients, with version history accessible via the "History" panel. REST API endpoints `/api/documents` and `/api/permissions` manage document lifecycles and access controls.  

## Contributing  
CollabSphere thrives on diverse input. To contribute:  
- File issues using the `bug`, `feature`, or `enhancement` templates  
- Submit PRs with tests covering edge cases (e.g., concurrent edits, network disruptions)  
- Follow the TypeScript style guide and ensure all components adhere to Web Components standards
